## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to patch multi-resource manifests and reason about rolling updates and resourcing in real deployments.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers for bootstrapping binaries
- PVC data paths and volume mounts
- Probes for correctness
- HorizontalPodAutoscaler and resource requests/limits
- PodDisruptionBudget for maintenance safety
- ConfigMap-triggered restarts via annotations

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: stream-processor
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/configqueue: queue-version-hash
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-binary
          image: alpine
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - wget -O /usr/local/bin/processor http://assets.local/processor.bin && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/processor
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data-input
              mountPath: /data/input
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: myregistry/stream-processor:latest
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
      volumes:
        - name: data-input
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: stream-processor-input
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design per-namespace automation with auditability and tight network controls. Image provenance is a critical security concern for multi-tenant environments like Discord or Airbnb, where ensuring container images come from trusted registries is essential.

## Key Concepts
- **CKAD Scheduling**: CronJob for recurring audit tasks
- **Image Provenance**: Registry API integration, image digests (SHA256)
- **Secrets & ConfigMaps**: REGISTRY_TOKEN for authentication, audit-status for state tracking
- **PV-backed Storage**: PVC at /audit for persistent digest reports
- **InitContainers**: Installing required tools (curl, jq) for image inspection
- **Readiness Probes**: Ensuring the pod is ready before accepting traffic
- **Namespace NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress to only trusted registries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-audit
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: audit-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
          containers:
          - name: auditor
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "..."]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
            - name: registry-token
              mountPath: /secrets
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "[ -f /audit/ready ]"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
          volumes:
          - name: audit-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: audit-pvc
          - name: registry-token
            secret:
              secretName: REGISTRY_TOKEN
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-status
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  last_run: ""
  digest_count: "0"
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: registry-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: registry
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **CronJob vs Job**: CronJob provides scheduling but has slight timing drift; use precise timing if required.
- **PVC Size**: Allocate sufficient storage based on pod count and audit frequency.
- **InitContainer Overhead**: Adds startup time but ensures tools are available; consider using a custom image with pre-installed tools.
- **NetworkPolicy Scope**: A permissive egress may be necessary if multiple registries are used; balance security with operational flexibility.
- **ConfigMap Updates**: Frequent updates may cause contention; consider annotation-based status or external database for high-frequency audits.

spec:

  selector:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: cache
spec:
  serviceName: cache-svc
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cache
    spec:
      initContainers:

        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo seed > /data/.seed"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data

      - name: cache
        image: redis:7
        ports:
        - containerPort: 6379
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:

          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:

          periodSeconds: 20

        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: cache-pvc

      name: cache

      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
---

kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: cache-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache

## Why This Is Asked
Auditors assess knowledge of Kubernetes pod security hardening and defense-in-depth strategies.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext vs container securityContext
- runAsNonRoot enforcement and UID requirements
- readOnlyRootFilesystem and volume mount implications
- Capability dropping and privilege escalation controls
- Seccomp profiles via annotations and runtime defaults
- Rolling update safety and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
# Security hardening patch for collector Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: collector
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod: runtime/default
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
        fsGroup: 2000
      containers:
      - name: collector
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - ALL
          volumeMounts:
          - name: input
            mountPath: /data/input
          - name: output
            mountPath: /data/output
        # Preserve existing probes and resources
        # livenessProbe, readinessProbe, resources remain unchanged
```

- Verify non-root execution: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- id`

- `kubectl rollout undo deployment/collector -n apps`
- Monitor rollout status: `kubectl rollout status deployment/collector -n apps`
- Document security context changes in version control
